paper_title: Counterfactual Influence as a Distributional Quantity
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how BLEU score changes over training epochs for three series labeled “Regular members,” “Members with near-duplicates,” and “Held-out data.” The x-axis is labeled “Epochs,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0 to 3 with regularly spaced tick labels every 0.5 (0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0). The y-axis is labeled “BLEU score,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 0.00 up to about 0.37 with tick labels at 0.05 intervals (0.00, 0.05, 0.10, …, 0.35). The “Regular members” series is a solid blue line with no markers; it starts near ~0.015 at the leftmost epoch, rises to around ~0.04–0.05 by roughly 0.5–0.8 epochs, reaches about ~0.06 around ~1.3 epochs, and then fluctuates slightly while trending upward to end near ~0.07 at 3.0 epochs. The “Members with near-duplicates” series is a solid orange line with no markers; it begins around ~0.02, increases steeply to about ~0.08 at 0.5 epochs, reaches roughly ~0.16–0.17 at 1.0 epochs and ~0.24–0.25 at 1.5 epochs, climbs to about ~0.34 around 2.0 epochs, and then varies slightly around ~0.33–0.36 before ending near ~0.37 at 3.0 epochs. The “Held-out data” series is a solid green line with no markers; it starts near ~0.025, rises to about ~0.04 by around 0.5 epochs, dips to roughly ~0.03 around ~0.7 epochs, returns to about ~0.04 around ~1.3–1.5 epochs, drops to roughly ~0.028 around ~1.8 epochs, and then oscillates around ~0.03–0.036 to finish near ~0.033 at 3.0 epochs.
